sources.author: Google Street View
observations: Near-frontal elevation (HC UK tenant). Three round-headed shop openings in a rendered ground storey; jettied first floor on a row of timber blocks; close-studded apron; two four-light leaded windows either side of a centre panel under a timber arch; tie beam with carved boss; gable with king post and nested chevron braces under heavy bargeboards.
North of the shop, beside NatWest, a narrow gated entrance bay with a small red-tiled roof over a set-back top window.
A dark open gap with a bin between the building and William Hill, with brick walls receding behind: the side alley. Used to scale widths and heights.

sources.author: Google Street View
observations: Oblique from the south: first floor and gable overhang the shopfront; the south return of the first floor is half-timbered.

sources.author: Google Street View
observations: Love To Eat tenant; sage-grey arched shop frames on a pale render storey. Red clay-tile main roof slope falls towards the alley; tall brick chimney behind; red-brick gabled ranges at the rear.
The alley opening between the cafe and William Hill is visible; William Hill's rendered side wall rises beside it.

sources.author: User-supplied reference from Google Maps
observations: Close view from the north: projecting left oriel stepping back through a canted centre to the right window; curved brace and small leaded window in the north bay; cast-iron bracket and railings at the gated entrance; bargeboard corner bracket; red brick and a wheelie bin in the alley mouth.

sources.author: Google satellite imagery
observations: Red clay-tile roof with its ridge running back from the street gable, a narrow red roof along the NatWest side, and a flat rooflit range behind. A dark strip separates the red roof from William Hill along the full range depth: the alley continues to the rear.

uncertainties: Street numbering: the user's link and Google's place name give 15 London St; Google's basemap shows an '8' label here and the old placeholder named the block 8. The asset uses 15.
Tenant lettering (HC UK 2011, Love To Eat 2020, SIP Southport in the current Google listing) is omitted rather than asserting present occupancy.
Ground-level alley width (1.32m) is a scaled estimate; any gate at the street end is not modelled because the 2011 and snag images show it open. The rear brick closure is estimated.
Range depth, roof pitch, bay roof form, chimney, rear range and all hidden elevations are estimates.
